To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

middle managers have an ambiguous role during organizational change; this ambiguity is due to the conflicting demands of their role; middle managers interpret the change and use this to inform their actions; this interpretation activity can be supported by the organization to reduce the conflict and ambiguity in the middle managers' role.

(1) middle managers are important to change implementation, but their role in this is often under-estimated; (2) they are often blamed for resistance to change, when in reality their role in change implementation is much more complex; and (3) they have the potential to play a crucial part in change, but to realize this potential they need support from their organization.
middle managers have a complex change intermediary role, which includes interpreting the change, implementing it and keeping their department going during the transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of middle managers in change.
how middle managers experience change.
the role of middle managers in the process of change implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings suggest that the role of middle managers in organizational change should be re-evaluated.
the role of the middle manager is to be a change intermediary, a change agent, an agent for change, an agent of change, a change agent and a change intermediary.
the role of middle management during organizational change is complex and multifaceted and requires careful management by both the organization and the individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
middle managers are a key resource in organizational change, but that their interpretation activity must be recognized if they are to be fully utilized.
middle managers are not the problem, they are the solution, but they need to be supported to fulfil their role.
middle managers are not simply the victims of organizational change, nor simply the agents of resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
middle managers are not a homogeneous group.
organizations should not underestimate the potential of middle managers to contribute to organizational change and transformation.
middle managers are a valuable organizational resource that can be harnessed for organizational transformation and change.
